analysis:
Both units are head-side excerpts of CHANGELOG.md, a documentation-only file (mode 100644 on both sides). The PR changes no executable code, config or workflow in the supplied excerpts, so it adds no runtime attack surface and no authorization, encryption, billing or availability regression. I checked the changelog's security-relevant claims against the canonical threat model.

- App Attest serving stays opt-in and disabled by default. Fresh assertions, build qualification, revocation checks and the connection binding are still required at every dispatch. This matches TB-011 and T-052 to T-058.
- Qualification of the exact signed artifact is described as separate from CI. This matches T-054.
- The SSD prefix-cache descriptions match T-041: the disk budget is half the available space with no fixed ceiling, there is a fixed 20 GiB reserve, and encryption and lookup identity checks are unchanged.
- Bonsai 2 SSD prefix-cache eligibility is described as on by default, but only for three exact supported identities. It is bounded by the global opt-out and the existing identity gates, so it stays within T-041's default-on, per-donation-gated posture.
- The privacy-description changelog entry says it removes unsupported memory-wiping and forward-secrecy claims. This makes the documentation more accurate and is consistent with T-003 and T-028.

I found no contradiction with the threat model. The excerpts do not show the underlying code, so the changelog's claims about behavior elsewhere in the repository are unverified here, and later passes should check them against the code diffs if any exist. The excerpts do not state the 30-minute TTL; they only describe the cache's other bounds, which agree with T-041.
